subject: Unified on-prem K8s footprint: node roles, PV classes & IO SLO decision log
messages:

Subject: Proposed unified footprint for on-prem deployment (questions)

Hi Marissa / Lauren,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. We sketched a few constraints on our side and wanted to get an explicit decision path for cluster shape and durable storage so procurement and infra can budget. High level constraints: air-gapped zone for model-serving clusters, limited central NFS (legacy) for stateful workloads, hardware mix across 6 sites (2x GPU heavy, 4x CPU-heavy), and HSM-backed KMS for keying.

Questions we need answered to proceed with PoC SOW:
- Node role breakdown (control / infra / GPU / batch) you recommend for a dual-tier footprint (edge + central).
- PV class recommendations: local SSD vs host-attached NVMe vs network-backed block (we have Ceph + NetApp).
- Snapshot / backup cadence expectations for model artifacts and KV cache persistence.
- Tolerances: recommended PVC eviction / reclaim policy for model-serving pods to meet 99.9% availability.

I attached an initial SOW draft. If you can provide a concise decision log we can lock the hardware quotes.

Thanks,
Alex Moreno
Solutions Architect | Solstice Systems

Subject: Decision log: cluster footprint, node roles, PV classes, and IO SLOs — PoC-ready

Alex — attaching the concise decision log and PV matrix per our cadence. Summary below so procurement can proceed.

Summary decisions (PoC defaults):
1) Cluster topology
- Central control plane (3 control-plane nodes, separate etcd PVs on network-backed block) located in the central data center.
- Edge model-serving clusters at each site (K=6): small control plane (3 nodes or stacked HA control-plane if there are hypervisor limits) + node pools per role.

2) Node pools (recommended default sizes for PoC)
- infra (logging/monitoring/ingress): 2-3 medium CPU nodes per site; tolerant of NFS for logs but prefer block for DBs.
- model-serving-gpu: 3-6 nodes in GPU sites (each node: 4 GPUs or equivalent); reserved for hot-serving; deploy with Guaranteed QoS class for core processes.
- model-serving-cpu: 6-8 nodes in CPU-heavy sites, used for replicas and batch decode workers.
- batch/cron: scaled-to-zero kubecron nodes (spot-like) for offline processing; isolated taints and nodeSelector.

3) PV classes and retention
- local-nvme: ephemeral local SSD for cache and KV cache (fastest). Retention: prefer rebuild-on-failure; use application-level replication for persistence.
- block-network (Ceph/NetApp): primary model artifact store (ReadWriteMany not required). Retention: 30d snapshot cadence by default for PoC; keep 7 daily + 6 weekly snapshots.
- nfs-legacy: allowed only for logs and tooling; not for model artifacts or KV cache.

4) IO SLOs and eviction policy
- Target 99.9% p95 latency for model-serving tail for 4k token sequences (benchmarking required per model).
- PVC reclaim policy: Retain for model-artifacts; Delete for ephemeral cache volumes. Use ReadWriteOnce for model-artifacts except when NetApp provides RWX-backed block.

5) Security / KMS
- HSM-backed KMS integration via an offline sync agent (no direct egress from air-gapped clusters). KMS secrets mirrored via signed bundle; rotation windows documented.

Attachments: pv-class-matrix.xlsx (decision matrix), io-slo-examples.md (SLO examples for team), solstice-sow-v2.pdf (updated SOW stub).

If this aligns, we recommend locking node counts and PV class choices into the SOW and purchasing temporary NVMe test nodes for the PoC to validate latency.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Decision log: cluster footprint, node roles, PV classes, and IO SLOs — PoC-ready

Marissa — this looks good and very actionable. A few clarifications before we finalize SOW:
- For the HSM/KMS approach, can you add language around signing the bundle and a 24-hour replay protection window? We need to show our security team the offline rotation model.
- For local-nvme as cache: confirm whether you expect the runtime to warm caches from network block on restart or if you expect replicated warm caches across nodes.
- Snapshot storage: can NetApp snapshots be used as the canonical backup (we want to avoid an extra object store).

We'll flag the PoC hardware list and push quotes next week once you sign off. Appreciate the speed.

Best,
Alex Moreno
Solutions Architect | Solstice Systems

> - For the HSM/KMS approach, can you add language around signing the bundle and a 24-hour replay protection window?
> - For local-nvme as cache: confirm whether you expect the runtime to warm caches from network block on restart or if you expect replicated warm caches across nodes.

Agree with Alex's asks. Quick ops notes / answers for the SOW:
- HSM/KMS: we'll add the signed bundle + monotonic counter and require the site agent to provide nonce proofs; recommended replay window 24h.
- NVMe cache warm: default behavior for PoC is warm-from-network (first deploy reads model artifact from block store into local NVMe), with optional cross-node cache replication as an advanced configuration.
- NetApp snapshots: allowed as canonical backup if retention policies and snapshot export controls meet compliance; we'll call this out as "Preferred canonical backup: NetApp snapshots (if available)".

I'll update the decision log with these clarifications and hand to Marissa for final copy into the SOW.

—Karthik
Head of Infrastructure Security | Redwood Inference
